tool.name: GeneralGridClassification
tool.summary: Classifies any single raster into categories using a saved 'general' classification system -- threshold rules on the grid's raw or whole-raster standardized (z-score) values. The same reusable classification systems and per-user store as the Slope Position and Landform tools, but for an arbitrary grid rather than a DEM. No Spatial Analyst extension.

usage.para: This is the general-purpose sibling of the Slope Position and Landform tools: it applies a saved classification system to ANY single-band raster (elevation, an index, a model output -- anything), turning continuous values into named, colored classes. It is the direct descendant of the "General Grid Classification" function in Jeff Jenness's ArcView 3 TPI extension.

Each class is defined by one or two threshold conditions on the input grid, interpreted either as RAW values (the grid's own units) or STANDARDIZED values (a whole-raster z-score, (value minus mean) divided by standard deviation). Raw thresholds are absolute; standardized thresholds adapt to the grid's own distribution -- useful when you do not know the value range in advance, or when comparing grids with different ranges. A cell takes a class when all of that class's conditions hold; where classes overlap, the lowest class value wins. Classification is a single vectorized pass in numpy, with no Esri Con or Spatial Analyst.

CLASSIFICATION SYSTEMS are reusable, named JSON rule sets (thresholds, names, colors) saved in a per-user location that survives add-in reinstalls. This tool lists the 'general' systems it finds there; the bundled defaults are a basic 4-class and 7-class template using standardized bands, meant as starting points to edit in the Classification System Builder. Per-class colors symbolize the output when it is added to the map. This tool supports systems that classify a single input grid.

dialogReference.para: Any single-band raster to classify. Its values are read as-is (for raw thresholds) or standardized whole-raster (for standardized thresholds), per the chosen classification system.

The output integer class raster, carrying a Value / Class_Name attribute table and a color map from the classification system. Cells matching no class (or outside the data) are unclassified. A name is suggested from the input.

The saved general classification system to apply (thresholds, names, colors). The list is read from the per-user store; the bundled defaults are basic 4-class and 7-class standardized-band templates. Author new systems with the Classification System Builder.

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Classify any single raster into categories using a saved classification system (raw or standardized threshold rules); no Spatial Analyst.
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Applies a saved 'general' classification system -- threshold rules (raw or whole-raster standardized values), class names, and colors -- to any single-band raster, producing an integer class raster with a Value/Class_Name attribute table and color map. Each class is an AND of one or two threshold conditions; the lowest class value wins on overlap. Classification is a single vectorized numpy pass with no Esri Con or Spatial Analyst. The reusable classification systems live in a per-user store that survives add-in reinstalls and are authored in the Classification System Builder; bundled defaults are basic 4- and 7-class standardized-band templates. Descends from the General Grid Classification function of Jenness's ArcView 3 TPI extension.
